recommendations.text: Check the appliance nameplate or manufacturer documentation for input power. If practical, use a suitable energy meter to measure actual consumption.
recommendations.safety_note: Do not open equipment or contact live electrical parts to obtain a reading.

recommendations.text: Review whether operating hours can be reduced or scheduled more efficiently without affecting essential use, food safety, comfort or manufacturer instructions.
recommendations.safety_note: Do not switch off essential medical, safety, refrigeration or other critical equipment.

recommendations.text: Where the manufacturer permits it and the device is not performing an essential function, consider its built-in standby or power-management settings.
recommendations.safety_note: Avoid cutting power to devices that require continuous operation, updates or safe shutdown.

recommendations.text: Compare verified energy labels or standardized manufacturer consumption figures for appliances providing the same service.
recommendations.safety_note: Compare like-for-like capacity, usage assumptions and label test conditions.

recommendations.text: Use the applicable marginal per-kWh rate from the current electricity tariff or bill and keep fixed charges and taxes separate.
recommendations.safety_note: A simplified estimate is not a guaranteed final bill amount.

recommendations.text: Stop using the affected appliance or outlet if it is safe to do so, keep others away, and contact a qualified electrician for inspection.
recommendations.safety_note: Do not touch exposed wires, attempt repairs, or repeatedly reset a tripping breaker.
